The *Paṭācārātherīapadāna* (Thi Ap 20) is a verse biographical account preserved in the Therīapadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the past lives, aspirations, and spiritual attainment of the elder nun Paṭācārā. Five translations across five modern languages are cataloged on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral records thematic and textual associations between the background of this account and verse collections across several Buddhist canons, noting cross-references to Pali Dhammapada verse 288, the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp 259–273, *Prakīrṇakavagga*), the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 358–375, *Māggavagga*), Chinese versions of the Dharmapada/Udāna literature (T 210.1, T 212.1, and T 213.1), and Sanskrit and Tibetan editions of the Udānavarga (*Anityavarga*) [SuttaCentral].
In DharmaNexus analysis, the text displays dense internal text reuse within Pali literature, registering 455 matching passages across 56 texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial sharing occurs with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, which contains 106 matches totaling more than 25,000 characters, most notably spanning segments §12.4–42.1 [DharmaNexus]. Substantial verse sharing also occurs with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and formulaic passages common across the Therīapadāna, especially the apadānas of Kisāgotamī (Thi-Ap 22), Dhammadinnā (Thi-Ap 23), Kuṇḍalakesā (Thi-Ap 21), Khemā (Thi-Ap 18), and Uppalavaṇṇā (Thi-Ap 19) [DharmaNexus].
